THREE OF FOUR FINDINGS INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED.
  F1 CONFIRMED both halves. The PR converts Write/Writev/Pwritev/Pwritev2 into
  syscalls::Pwritev2 with RWF_APPEND (files.rs 2042/2091/2098/2105). The pinned Reverie
  8c8c0a57 reverie-kvm/src/executor.rs is 23,607 lines and contains ZERO case-insensitive
  matches for pwritev2; positive control pwrite matches, SYS_write at 299, SYS_writev at
  303, SYS_pwrite64 at 313, fn pwrite64 at 2678, terminal else negative_errno(ENOSYS) at
  829. My FIRST query returned zero for query and control both -- measuring nothing --
  because the spelling is libc::SYS_*, not the variant names. Re-ran with a working
  control.
  F2 CONFIRMED. prepare_backend_config sets discover_live_file_metadata = (backend ==
  Sabre); tool_local.rs:2328 branches on it, calls discover_fd_from_current_process for
  fds 0..=2 and returns a literal None alias error. SaBRe never reaches setup_stdio,
  same_description, or the new fail-closed alias semantics.
  F4 CONFIRMED BY RUNNING. Built a program against the pinned nix 0.30.1 and libc
  0.2.189: libc::O_LARGEFILE = 0x0, OFlag::O_LARGEFILE.bits() = 0x0,
  from_bits_truncate(0x8001) -> 0x0001 LOST BITS, 0x8401 -> 0x0401 LOST BITS. So the
  model cannot represent 0x8000 and the newly authoritative F_GETFL returns the
  truncated word. This bears on the change's OWN evidence: an earlier comment reports
  "containment probe 0x8001 -> 0x8001 contained", which cannot be the model-backed
  F_GETFL for a contained descriptor.
  F3 NOT VERIFIED -- the DBT fork/exec lifetime finding. Neither confirmed nor disputed.

Two corrections to the dispatch's premise, both measured.

1. "Never reviewed / nothing is known about it" is not right. PR 2694 carries 29
   comments, including multiple reviewer-tagged rounds, three adversarial-reviewer
   comments, and an exact-head reconstruction review. It has been looked at a great
   deal. What is true is that the current head has no recorded VERDICT that a reader
   can find, which is a different and more interesting problem -- see below.

2. The gate does not report this pull request as blocked. It reports
   INDETERMINATE, rc=2:

     changes-requested-gate: INDETERMINATE pr=2694 head=46670790208e
       -- review event order is unreadable:
          APPROVED-AT<retracted> claude <a FABRICATED sha, see below>.
          A retirement cannot be credited without the immutable refusal and
          withdrawal times

CAUSE, established in the code rather than inferred. approval_binding.py
unresolved_review_objections() runs lane_shas() for each lane collecting malformed
markers, and then:

    if malformed:
        detail = "; ".join(sorted({message for _where, message in malformed}))
        raise ReviewRecordError(detail)

That raise happens BEFORE any unresolved objection is returned. So a single
malformed marker-shaped line anywhere in the thread discards the entire objection
computation for every head.

The offending line is at column 0, unfenced, at the end of comment 5429972968
(2026-08-26): `APPROVED-AT<retracted> claude <a FABRICATED sha, see below>`. Its
author was retracting an approval whose sha they had fabricated -- the retraction
itself is honest, but writing it as a marker-shaped line is what jams the gate.
lane_shas names that comment as the malformed record for BOTH lanes.

WHAT IT HIDES, measured by a controlled experiment at the library layer. Fencing
that ONE line in that ONE comment and changing nothing else,
unresolved_review_objections returns 6 unresolved refusals:

    claude 7fc9417bdf47   (outrun)
    claude 446667cf0765   (outrun)
    codex  c48492260889   (outrun)
    codex  19e884d65fcf   (outrun)
    codex  f6d7aac97b85   (outrun)
    codex  46670790208e   <-- BINDS THE EXACT CURRENT HEAD

A NEGATIVE RESULT I ALMOST REPORTED AS POSITIVE, recorded because it changes the
remedy. My first attempt fenced the string in BOTH comments that contain it --
5429972968 and 5429980495, which quotes it in prose. That still raised. The
quotation comment already contains fenced blocks, and inserting another fence
there flips its parity and re-surfaces the line. Fencing ONLY the originating
comment clears it. So the remedy is one targeted edit, not a sweep for the string.

CONSEQUENCE. A lander reading rc=2 sees "unreadable", not "blocked by six refusals,
one of which binds your head". INDETERMINATE reads as a tooling problem. This is
why a pull request with 29 comments and a live at-head refusal can sit twenty days
looking like it is merely waiting.

# Inherited-status transaction design against immutable 466707902

Target: https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/2694 at **46670790208e71be0b1aa0e249297c0f4b38663a**, based on dade02611a0988aaa2f234411c16462fdbfb5519. Dependency source is the actually pinned Reverie **8c8c0a57649c9ffbf8a7a14291a64320f64b935f**. This is read-only design following the changes-requested full review, not approval of an implementation. No tests, builds, guests, product edits, index/ref/object mutations, or public changes were performed for this task. Only this evidence directory and the authorized verified umbrella note were written. Moving stdio working files were not used as the source base.

## Result and concrete limits

Use one run-owned inherited-status authority, indexed by the existing stable OpenFileId, with descriptor-table bindings indexed by FilesId and incarnation. A status-changing operation must own its physical completion independently of the guest response. An unowned Begin/guest injection/Finish RPC pair is insufficient: current terminal RPC fencing can prevent Finish after the kernel effect occurred. A mutex held across guest injection, or an assumed Device resource lock, does not fix this.

The coordinator's simpler alternative—retaining an exact duplicate descriptor and performing the physical F_SETFL plus logical commit inside the authority—solves that completion-ownership problem for a proven physical capability. It is **not already supplied by current backend setup**, and cannot be implemented as “dup supervisor fd 0/1/2 and retain until run cleanup.” Captured OS pipe ends, PTYs, actual reserved stdin, synthetic KVM capture, and last-close semantics make that shortcut incorrect. The exact missing hooks are listed below.

There are three separable implementation interfaces: (1) shared logical state and incarnation-bound fd bindings, (2) owned physical status effects with record/replay accounting, and (3) backend descriptor identity/lifetime reporting. The first is useful in all backends; it does not make the other two optional. No additional transport protocol or test implementation is proposed here. API names below describe required internal operations using the existing Tool/global-RPC/backend ownership structure.

## Existing ordering: what can actually be reused

All line references below name retained immutable source copies under `source/` or `dependency/`, not a changing checkout.

* `detcore/src/scheduler.rs:3857` immediately grants Device/FileContents/FileMetadata and the other ordinary resources; it does not acquire an OFD lock. `tool_global.rs:1458` and `1463` release functions only trace. `tool_global.rs:2618` returns Normal without an RPC when sequentialize_threads is false. Therefore neither Permission::W nor release_resources excludes a concurrent status update.
* There **is** real serialized-turn exclusion: scheduler `check_request`/`are_all_quiesced` at 1699–1725 waits for every runnable thread's request; `step1_check_quiescence` at 4030 calls that check; `unblock_guest` at 4249 clears the selected thread's request before publishing its response. The daemon cannot grant another ordinary turn until the selected thread parks again. `BlockingExternalIO` deliberately removes that thread from this set. This exclusion follows the request/quiescence protocol, not Device identity.
* `recv_request_resources` at `tool_global.rs:1341` publishes a request, drops the scheduler mutex, awaits the response, then rechecks incarnation/logical death. The same short-lock/await-outside-lock pattern is reusable for a status operation's completion wait.
* `receive_rpc` at 795–889 rejects stale or tombstoned callers before dispatch, and 1290–1339 rechecks terminal state after awaited dispatch. `send_and_update_time` at 2565 maps ThreadExited to tail-injected Exit instead of returning to the operation. A final guest RPC cannot be the sole physical-completion record.
* `pre_handler_hook` at `detcore/src/lib.rs:570` can end a timeslice, but is not an unconditional admission for each syscall. A new control operation must establish or carry an actual normal-turn admission; it cannot infer one from “this is a syscall callback.”
* `GlobalState::initialize` starts the scheduler only in serialized configurations. StartNewThread/CreateChildThread helper calls are conditional on serialization, and `recv_deregister_thread:1788` asserts serialization. A status registry needed in nonserialized ptrace/SaBRe/KVM must register/retire through an unconditional lifecycle path, without invoking that assertion or treating a missing scheduler incarnation as proof: `rpc_incarnation_matches:2044` currently accepts a missing map entry. Hermit's DBT front door already rejects nonserialized mode (`hermit-cli/src/lib.rs:2148`); this repair need not invent DBT support for that mode.

## Minimum authority state and API

| State or operation | Concrete meaning and invariant |
| --- | --- |
| InheritedDescription[OpenFileId] | Raw logical F_GETFL word (i32, retaining unknown bits), observed physical word, monotone status version, exact physical or synthetic backend capability, and counts of guest bindings / admitted control operations. Store only inherited-description status here; do not replace inode, offset, socket or flock models globally. |
| Binding[(FilesId, fd)] | OpenFileId, descriptor-local FD_CLOEXEC, and binding generation. An fd number or inode is not identity. The same OpenFileId can appear at arbitrary fd numbers and in multiple forked tables. A shared CLONE_FILES table has one table identity, not one reference per thread. |
| Actor[(DetTid, MmId)] | Explicit live incarnation and descriptor table. Validate old/new exec transitions against the existing pending-exec record. Nonserialized operation still requires a real registration. |
| Control operation | Unique operation identity tied to actor, table binding generation and OpenFileId; queued/started/terminal state; original requested raw word; actual effect result; resulting version. A repeated delivery retrieves the same completion, never repeats the kernel update. |
| RegisterInherited / BindAliases | Backend supplies proven capability and the actual root alias classes. Register atomically after all identity checks, before guest effects. Do not publish a partially checked stdio table. |
| ReadStatus | Validate actor and binding; wait for an already-started same-description control to finish; return one complete versioned snapshot. No lease remains after reply. |
| SetStatus | Validate/admit, own the short control effect, read physical word, enforce existing supported-change and physical-append-clear refusals, update only physical O_NONBLOCK when required, then publish logical and physical state together. Guest delivery is separate from completion ownership. |
| BeginProbe / CompleteProbe | Only if a physical nonblocking probe needs exclusion against physical mode changes beyond proven serialized-turn ownership. Permit covers one already-classified nonblocking injection, never a blocking operation or polling loop. Completion must be recorded by the backend's execution owner or proven physical exit, not exclusively by a guest Finish. |
| Bind/Unbind/PrepareExec/Reconnect/Cancel | Update binding identity/lifetime on actual kernel outcomes. These are extensions of current lifecycle handling, not permission to derive success from a request being sent. |

A mutex protects only table transitions. It is released before waiting, injecting, doing filesystem work, or acquiring scheduler/metadata locks. Per-description queued operations own their result slot and capability; the global handler may await the slot without owning the operation. The operation runner continues after cancellation of its waiter. No blocking MutexGuard crosses an await. Different descriptions can progress independently.

In serialized mode, obtain the existing resource admission before publishing a status effect; preserve the one-resource request invariant (`scheduler.rs:3674`). The actual operation is ordered by that grant. Waiting for an already-admitted owner must not require another guest to receive a turn: the owner is the independent authority/backend effect runner. Do not admit queued background guest effects merely because RPC arrival happened first. In nonserialized mode, the same authority queue remains active, and overlapping controls linearize through it; this mode does not promise deterministic host-arrival ordering.

## F_SETFL transaction, errors and cancellation

`syscalls/files.rs:2895–2990` currently reads logical state, invokes nested-tool F_GETFL, possibly invokes nested-tool F_SETFL, updates physical cached nonblocking, then updates logical flags. Those separate awaits are the interval the new authority must close.

1. At actual syscall admission, resolve the current fd binding and retain its OpenFileId for this operation. Validate the actor and table generation. Preserve invalid-fd/kernel errno precedence; advisory metadata discovery is not permission to invent a different guest error.
2. Enqueue the control while holding only the short authority lock. Same-description ReadStatus, another SetStatus, and conflicting physical nonblocking probes wait outside that lock. Ordinary already-issued I/O does not wait and holds no status lease.
3. The owned runner reads the actual physical word through its proven capability. Evaluate `unsupported_contained_status_flag_change` against the current authority logical word, preserving the EOPNOTSUPP cases. Preserve the current refusal of clearing logical append while physical O_APPEND remains set.
4. Construct physical_next from the newly read **physical** word with only O_NONBLOCK replaced. Never use the guest's complete logical word to change the supervisor description. If no physical bit change is needed, there is no physical F_SETFL. Preserve the raw logical non-settable bits.
5. On actual success, publish the physical observation and `(logical_before & !SETTABLE_STATUS_FLAGS) | (requested & SETTABLE_STATUS_FLAGS)` in one authority transition, advance its version, and retain the terminal result. Then wake waiters. The client cache becomes a versioned copy, not the authority.
6. On an actual kernel/refusal error, publish no logical success; retain the real error and complete the operation before releasing exclusion. An uncertain physical result is not “errno with old state restored.” It keeps the operation unresolved until its execution owner supplies an actual result or an authenticated reconciliation is possible. No guessed rollback.
7. Only after completion is published does the guest response flow through normal incarnation checks. A terminal caller may receive ThreadExited while another live alias still sees the completed status. This is not resurrection of the dead guest.

| Cancellation boundary | Required action |
| --- | --- |
| Before effect admission/start | Remove queued request, release its temporary identity reference, no physical/logical update. |
| After owned effect starts, before result | Cancel response delivery only. Runner retains capability and completes. Neither Drop nor logical death pretends the syscall failed. |
| After physical success, before logical publication | Same owner must finish publication. No guest Finish is required. |
| After publication, before response | Keep committed state/result; terminal RPC fencing can suppress only delivery. |
| Guest physical exit while a guest-owned probe is active | A backend completion or exact physical-exit witness ends that probe. A logically killed flag alone does not prove the kernel stopped reading or changing the description. |
| Authority/backend failure with unknown effect | Preserve uncertainty and fail the run's infrastructure/evidence path; do not return PASS, old flags, or silently unlock for a competing update. This is an actual-failure rule, not a new broad execution gate. |

The Begin/guest-inject/Finish alternative needs the same independent completion witness. Calling Finish from a Rust destructor is not possible asynchronously; permitting a tombstoned guest to send a generic Finish would also bypass current incarnation guards. An internal backend completion keyed by the already admitted operation is distinct from reviving an old guest RPC.

### Capability lifetime is part of correctness

A permanent extra descriptor changes last-close behavior. For a pipe writer it prevents EOF; for a retained reader it can prevent EPIPE; PTY child handles similarly prevent EOF (`pty.rs:37`). A retained regular description may extend an OFD lock's lifetime. Descriptor references cannot just live until GlobalState cleanup.

This is visible in current real call ordering: ptrace `wait_with_output:1480–1506` joins wait with both drains before yielding the GlobalState; DBT `wait_with_output:717–766` waits for status then joins readers; SaBRe `run_blocking:1035–1057` runs the supervisor then joins readers. Holding a captured child write end until those functions return can make them never return. SaBRe does have an earlier physical exit callback at `sabre_ptrace.rs:370`, but it currently accounts for scheduler process exit, not an authority OFD reference.

An authority capability must therefore be dropped when the last actual guest alias disappears and every already-admitted finite control/probe reference completes. Count tables/aliases, not just tasks or root fd 0/1/2. Track dup/dup2 replacement/dup3/F_DUPFD, close, close_range, fork/CLONE_FILES, successful exec CLOEXEC drops, and physical exit. Account for captured references already present in `CapturedDetFd`. For close/replacement, a cancellation between successful kernel operation and the current local metadata callback is another completion-witness problem: keeping an extra reference until a guessed cleanup event changes observable EOF. A final physical process-exit report can resolve all its remaining bindings, but waiting until exit is insufficient if the program closes stdout and then waits for its consumer before exit. Thus the retained-descriptor approach is a concrete option, not a smaller patch that bypasses lifecycle integration.

## Record/replay boundary that the central alternative must retain

`Detcore::record_or_replay` at `tool_local.rs:373` calls the actual nested Tool with a Guest. The current contained F_SETFL sends physical F_GETFL and conditional physical F_SETFL through it. Recorder routes fcntl to `handle_simple` (`recorder.rs:578/1352`), actually injects, and records Return. Replayer routes ordinary fcntl to `handle_simple` (`replayer.rs:512/1954`) and consumes Return without injecting. F_SETFD and duplication use separate side-effect paths.

A central libc::fcntl therefore cannot be swapped in while claiming the current nested-tool path is unchanged. The narrow integration point is an owned-effect adapter for these specific inherited-status operations: preserve the same event positions and actual result/error distinctions; let the authority own physical completion rather than an anonymous future in a dead guest. Replay must consume recorded outcomes exactly once and distinguish replay state from actually materialized host/synthetic capability state. It must not set `physically_nonblocking=true` merely because a recorded F_SETFL returned zero, or push the guest's whole logical word to a replay host file. The immutable RecordOrReplay trait is only a Tool bound and currently exposes no such owned-effect adapter. Designing that adapter is required implementation work, not an existing API we can assert is present.

The append write paths must continue to reach Recorder/Replayer with the current WriteV2 operands and strict bytes/offset behavior. The nine passing ptrace stdio cases and the retained append regression do not qualify a new central-physical implementation. The unchanged general fcntl replay behavior above is an integration constraint, not a newly claimed independent regression from this PR.

1. Implement the shared inherited identity/status registry and extend the existing incarnation-bound exec/fork handoff, leaving the independently assigned SaBRe root alias/raw-word correction separate. Local Arc remains a cache/alias helper, never cross-process authority.
2. Choose and implement one actual owned-effect route. Retained exact capabilities are preferable to a cancelled-guest Finish for F_SETFL, **only after** final backend stdio binding and timely alias/close retirement are supplied. Synthetic KVM capture must use its actual backend representation. Otherwise the guest-injection route needs an independent backend syscall-completion owner; the current generic RPC guards cannot substitute.
3. Wire all readers above. Hold no status lease over blocking I/O, a resource wait, exec, or an entire retry loop. Keep short-probe physical guarantees and cancellation explicit, and preserve the record/replay front door rather than bypassing it.

This is the minimal API/state proposal, with the exact unavailable capabilities exposed. It is not a claim that all required backend hooks fit in a one-file transaction helper. 3. Put inherited status authority outside copied Tool address spaces and restore its identity through exec.

A local Arc alone cannot repair the DBT defect. The existing GlobalState already lives in the central Tool/coordinator process (tool_global.rs:404 onward), survives external Tool clients, and stores pending exec state keyed by deterministic process identity. Local DetFd values may remain caches, but they cannot remain the authority. F_GETFL, F_SETFL and every operation consulting inherited append or nonblocking state must obtain a current snapshot at its actual admitted operation point. The status operation must be serialized as an OFD operation, not ordered by arrival at a new RPC mutex. For deterministic execution, use the existing canonical inherited Device resource/admitted continuation and the same description ID across aliases. The exact transaction API still needs implementation review: F_SETFL's physical update and logical commit must not interleave inconsistently with another operation on the same description. Findings

1. P1 — Ordinary redirected KVM write/writev now reaches an unimplemented Pwritev2 dispatch arm.

At detcore/src/syscalls/files.rs:2018–2115, record_or_replay_inherited_write translates an ordinary Write or Writev on logically append-mode inherited regular output into Pwritev2(offset=-1, RWF_APPEND). The containment policy intentionally leaves the host OFD's O_APPEND bit clear. The conversion is reached by handle_write and handle_writev after their existing resource admission; it is not restricted to guests explicitly requesting a positioned syscall.

The complete real path is hermit-cli/src/lib.rs:1944–2130 (run_kvm, including run_static_elf_with_tool::<Detcore> at 2093), Detcore::init_thread_state, ThreadState::new/setup_stdio's host fstat, the changed write handlers, then the Tool guest's nested injection. Cargo.lock pins Reverie to 8c8c0a57649c9ffbf8a7a14291a64320f64b935f. In that exact source, reverie-kvm/src/runtime.rs:495–498 calls executor.execute; executor.rs:2070–2140 dispatches to execute_basic_syscall_with_output. Its match at 299–320 implements Write, Writev and Pwrite64, but has no Pwritev2 arm anywhere in the executor. The fallback at 830 returns ENOSYS. The original Write path at 2296–2350 does support ordinary host stdout output.

Concrete trigger: provide stdout as a regular file at an offset before EOF, let the guest successfully set O_APPEND, then call ordinary write(1, ...). The new implementation returns ENOSYS through the pinned executor instead of appending. This is a regression of ordinary write, not merely the pre-existing absence of a guest Pwritev2 syscall. Captured synthetic-FIFO output is a different path and does not disprove this regular-host-output trigger. The new run_kvm_guest_cannot_mutate_hermits_stdout_flags test preserves the right prefix/output/status oracle, but the actual portable campaign filtered KVM tests; it never qualified this case.

Required change: integrate an actual supported append implementation into the executor used by this PR, or another coherent backend implementation of the same contract. The disclosed dependency on https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/538 is not present at the pinned executor and does not fix this head. Preserve host and captured-output distinctions, the original ordinary-write assertion, error and offset semantics, and containment. Do not forward the guest's full physical status word or exclude KVM. After repair, the existing ordinary-write KVM control plus relevant host/capture cases are the focused runtime evidence needed; no universal full-profile gate is proposed.

2. P1 — SaBRe bypasses inherited-OFD alias discovery, so contained flags split one Linux description into independent models.

hermit-cli/src/lib.rs:2327 sets discover_live_file_metadata for Backend::Sabre. ThreadState::new at detcore/src/tool_local.rs:2328–2340 takes a different branch for that configuration: it calls discover_fd_from_current_process separately for fd 0, 1 and 2 and returns no alias error. It never calls the new setup_stdio_with/kcmp path. discover_fd_from_current_process at 720–756 calls add_fd, whose 780–792 implementation allocates a new OpenFileId and DetFd/Arc for each descriptor. A later with_detfd does not rediscover an existing descriptor. The actual pinned experimental/reverie-sabre/src/reverie_adapter.rs:419–425 constructs Detcore from this config and calls init_thread_state(tid, None) for a fresh root.

Concrete trigger: inherited stdout and stderr are dup aliases, as with 2>&1. Guest F_SETFL(stdout, O_APPEND) changes only stdout's logical description. The new F_GETFL(stderr) reads its separate cached description and omits O_APPEND; a subsequent ordinary stderr write does not take the append conversion and can overwrite the file at its current offset. Before this change the physical shared OFD supplied these flags. Sharing Arc values on the normal setup_stdio path does not repair the branch SaBRe actually uses.

Required change: preserve inherited description equivalence in the SaBRe initialization/discovery route too, while retaining its live descriptor type and nonblocking behavior and the new fail-closed alias-error semantics. A control must exercise the real discover_live_file_metadata configuration with duplicated descriptors and independent opens of the same inode; testing only setup_stdio_with is insufficient. No SaBRe execution was performed in this review.

3. P1 — DBT's contained status state has the wrong lifetime across real fork and exec.

The new logical status resides in OpenFileDescription behind a process-local Arc<Mutex<...>> (detcore/src/fd.rs:207–230, set_logical_status_flags at 654). FileMetadata::fork_for shares that Arc among modeled processes within a single address space; FileMetadata::for_exec retains descriptions in the ordinary hosted Tool path. Those mechanisms do not cover DBT's actual copied or replaced address spaces.

For normal DBT fork, detcore-dbt/src/lib.rs:1336–1395 explicitly takes the copied DynamoRIO process's copy-on-write parent allocation and initializes the child's state from it. The pinned native client has actual normal-fork lifecycle handling; the refusals for unsupported CLONE_FILES/CLONE_VM combinations do not refuse ordinary fork. reverie_dbt_runtime_process_clone_result at 1593–1623 explicitly acknowledges independently mutable copied state and invalidates flock knowledge, but does not move status flags into a shared authority or synchronize them. After a child successfully sets contained O_APPEND, the parent's model is unchanged. Following wait or another deterministic synchronization, the parent reports stale F_GETFL and can write without append. A process-local Arc is not cross-process OFD storage. Forwarded O_NONBLOCK can similarly leave another copied model stale.

For exec, the native lifecycle branch at detcore-dbt/src/lib.rs:2175–2210 calls send_dbt_prepare_exec (474–505) and then delegates the actual exec. That message carries identity/mm and an empty BTreeSet, not logical inherited-OFD status. The new native image initializes fresh per-thread scratch (pinned client.c:3943) and a fresh root Tool state; setup_stdio can recover only the unchanged physical flags. Guest-set logical O_APPEND disappears across successful exec even for an inherited descriptor without FD_CLOEXEC. The normal in-process for_exec helper is not the path that preserves this state in DBT.

These are new consequences of replacing the kernel OFD's flag authority with a local model; the pre-existing copied runtime by itself is not a sufficient explanation for accepting them. Required change: give logical inherited-OFD state an authority/lifetime shared by actual fork descendants and carry it through successful exec reconnect, preserving descriptor aliases and close-on-exec behavior. Add focused child-set/parent-observe-and-write and set-then-exec controls through the real DBT paths. Preserve physical containment, successful ordinary fork/exec semantics and scheduler ordering. No DBT guest run was performed to infer this finding. The author confirmed no existing repair or status handoff path was known; the source trace is the basis for the finding.

4. P2 — Model-backed F_GETFL can lose an immutable raw status bit during initialization.

setup_stdio_with at detcore/src/tool_local.rs:666 and the live discovery branch at 742 construct OFlag with from_bits_truncate(status_flags). The newly authoritative F_GETFL at detcore/src/syscalls/files.rs:2868–2880 then returns the stored bits instead of the kernel word. In the retained nix 0.30.1 source, OFlag enumerates libc constants; GNU 64-bit libc 0.2.189 defines O_LARGEFILE as zero (gnu/b64/mod.rs:194), whereas the Linux UAPI raw O_LARGEFILE is octal 00100000 (0x8000). Thus a raw inherited regular-file word such as the implementation's own retained historical 0x8001 example becomes 0x1 in this model. The access mode survives, but exact F_GETFL observability does not. This narrower issue is independent of the three blockers and was not newly run.

Preserve the complete raw initial status word, excluding only descriptor-local flags that really are separate, and apply the five-bit F_SETFL mask when modifying it. Include a full-word initialization assertion using a raw bit not represented by the platform OFlag constants. Source copies and provenance limits are in raw-status-word-source-binding.json: package versions match Cargo.lock, but this retained Cargo source directory has no per-file .cargo-checksum.json, so I do not claim a fresh package-integrity verification for these copies. The installed Linux header is a reference, not a guest build observation.

  reflog names the actual mechanism:

    129ea65fe refs/heads/main@{2026-09-13 07:44:25 -0700}: merge origin/main: Fast-forward

  Something fast-forwards this ref every one to two hours. Local time is UTC-7,
  so the 10:44:11 entry is 17:44:11Z -- inside my measurement window, between my
  two reads. The ref had last synced at 14:44:25Z, so the three-hour gap that
  read as "held for three checks" is the interval between two syncs.

  The practical consequence is unchanged and worth keeping: a reader who takes
  landing state from refs/heads/main in this checkout can be up to a sync
  interval behind and will report no progress when progress has occurred. Every

P1: reverie-kvm/src/executor.rs:3857–3863 applies the one-iovec optimization to every vector count. decode_guest_iovecs validates min(entry.length, MAX_RW_COUNT) for every entry. Linux's multi-segment __import_iovec instead checks access_ok against each original length before applying the aggregate clamp. Only the nr_segs==1 path goes through import_ubuf, which clamps before access_ok. For two vectors such as [(valid_mapped_prefix, SSIZE_MAX), (NULL, 0)], the full first range fails Linux's access_ok. The current decoder accepts its shortened range and can forward a staged accessible prefix through vectored_io (4106, 4176–4203).

The assertion at executor.rs:16836–16849 encodes this defect: it supplies two vectors [(DATA, isize::MAX), (DATA, 1)], unwraps successful decoding, and expects the bounded prefix. Its comment incorrectly generalizes the single-entry rule.

Preserve signed-length checks, validation of all remaining vectors after the aggregate cap, guest-fd translation, endpoint error ordering and bounded supervisor allocation. Exercise the actual executor for one/two-entry SSIZE_MAX-1 and SSIZE_MAX neighbors with bounded mapped prefixes; check return/errno, bytes and offsets, including no write or read consumption on the rejected multi-entry range. Source assessment for https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/2694: F_DUPFD_QUERY.

The retained GitHub contents responses were fetched through with-proxy from torvalds/linux at tag v7.1; every command preserves UTC, status, duration, stderr, raw response, decoded source bytes and Git blob identity. This is upstream source, not a byte match to the custom host kernel or proof of runtime availability.

include/uapi/linux/fcntl.h:18 defines F_DUPFD_QUERY as F_LINUX_SPECIFIC_BASE+3, or 1027. fs/fcntl.c:587 resolves the first descriptor using fd_raw, returns EBADF if absent, permits this command on O_PATH, and invokes security_file_fcntl. do_fcntl at463 dispatches to f_dupfd_query. That function at396 resolves and holds the second descriptor with fd_raw, returns EBADF if absent, and returns fd_file(f) == filp. Thus success is exactly one for the same open file description and zero for a different description. This is the reverse of kcmp's equal=zero interpretation. The kernel compares struct file identity, not inode/offset/status equality and does not allocate another descriptor or change either file's flags/position.

Unlike kcmp it has no PID namespace lookup, cross-task exec-update lock or ptrace-access check. It is an exact same-process alternative for these current-host stdio comparisons. It still crosses the fcntl LSM/security hook and any syscall filter; EINVAL/EPERM/EBADF and any other error are not inequality. The first and second held descriptors exist for the comparison, but this does not itself freeze unrelated userspace close/replacement between an earlier fstat/F_GETFL and the query. The current inherited-stdio setup already assumes those supervisor descriptors remain stable during initialization; extending arbitrary concurrently replaced descriptors would require a distinct identity-lifetime design.

A bounded compatibility choice is to prefer the exact query, accept only its documented zero/one success, and retain refusal on all unknown results. A legacy-kernel fallback can attempt kcmp only after an explicitly documented unsupported-query outcome; if that exact comparison succeeds it supplies the proof, and if it fails the diagnostic must retain the failed operation and fd/errno evidence. There is no sound fallback to inode equality, assuming distinct descriptors, assuming all aliases, or modifying status flags to infer sharing. If a native supported-query probe is authorized, it must distinguish duplicate from independent opens of the same inode, same-fd identity, invalid left/right fd, unchanged offset/flags, and a deliberate denied-query path. No such probe has run from this lane, and the source-only fallible-kcmp candidate includes no fallback.

P1: detcore/src/syscalls/files.rs:2846 removes the existing logical O_NONBLOCK mask for every non-stdio descriptor. The new inherited-stdio branch returns the modeled word correctly, but its remaining F_GETFL path now directly returns the physical kernel word. The same head's handle_pipe2 at3407–3420 and3480–3486 deliberately creates a physically nonblocking guest pipe while registering the guest's original flags. Its F_SETFL path at2943–2963 likewise forces physical O_NONBLOCK for scheduler-managed sockets, pipes and eventfds while preserving the requested logical flags. Therefore a guest-created blocking pipe followed by F_GETFL now exposes O_NONBLOCK even though the caller did not request it; F_SETFL(fd,0) also cannot hide the internal flag on these descriptors. This is a direct regression from the base's explicit logical-bit masking and contradicts the description's claim that guest-opened descriptors are unchanged. Restore the original logical mask in the non-stdio branch, keeping the modeled whole-word return only for inherited stdio. A meaningful control should check guest-created pipe flags before and after F_SETFL plus dup aliases, with native expected flags and the unchanged inherited-stdio cases. No runtime failure is claimed from this source inference.

P1 requiring a focused scheduler witness: detcore/src/syscalls/files.rs:2089 and2299 seek inherited append-mode streams to EOF BEFORE resource_request at2101 and2311. resource_request in detcore/src/tool_global.rs:2575–2601 submits RequestResources and awaits a scheduler response when threads are sequentialized. A sibling using the same open file description can therefore move the shared offset between this seek and the actual write/writev. Native O_APPEND chooses EOF atomically at the write, so a prior lseek by the sibling cannot redirect the write; this implementation can instead overwrite existing bytes. The new seek must be inside the serialized actual-write interval, after scheduling admission, or use an appropriate atomic per-call append mechanism while preserving each syscall's offset semantics. Do not solve this by adding a comparator relaxation or excluding concurrent aliases. ## Why APPROVE

The trigger-4 change is ~185 lines in detcore/src/scheduler.rs; the other 1,200+ lines are CI harness.
`complete_physical_process_exit` now only RECORDS into a new `reported_physical_process_exits` set,
and only the scheduler applies it, at the top of `sched_loop_inner` (scheduler.rs:1157-1158)
immediately before the completion check. That makes `pending_physical_process_exits` immutable for a

## Three findings

1. **BLOCKING, liveness.** `start_pending_thread` (reverie-dbt/native/client.c:1534-1544) spins
   `dr_sleep(1)` with no deadline, no diagnostic and no `exit_runtime_tree` until the parent
   publishes the thread mapping. The same unbounded loop is now also on the syscall path at
   client.c:3868-3872, where a `!has_copied_runtime() &&` guard was removed, so it covers more
   threads than before. Because the pending counter is per-virtual-process, one stuck clone blocks
   every later thread of that process, and the symptom is a silent hang with no output naming why.
   The bounded idiom already exists inside the same function: the test path at client.c:2097-2106
   gives up after 1000 attempts and calls exit_runtime_tree(93). Apply that to the production wait.

   I traced the decrement paths BEFORE raising this rather than assuming a leak, and they are
   correct: `pending_virtual_child` is assigned from `allocate_virtual_identity()` at client.c:2021
   before the increment at client.c:2047, that allocator never returns 0, so the `virtual_child == 0`
   early return at client.c:2073 cannot strand a counted clone; and `finish_pending_thread_clone`
   runs for `result != 0`, which covers failed clones as the description claims. What is unbounded is
   the WAIT, whose safety rests entirely on the parent always reaching its post-hook -- an invariant
   nothing asserts.

   ⚠️ This is the SAME defect shape the predecessor found on
   https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/2747: an unbounded wait with no terminal report. Twice in
   this queue of ten. Worth treating as a pattern.

2. **Needs an explicit owner decision, not a silent landing.** The entry-block clean call is now
   UNCONDITIONAL (client.c:1589-1595): the previous `pending_thread_starts != 0` gate is gone, so
   every basic block of every guest carries a full-application-context `dr_insert_clean_call_ex`
   forever, to reach a callee that returns immediately in the common case. The description honestly
   discloses the cost: a two-million-iteration loop went 0.057806s -> 0.112805s median over five
   alternating runs, about 1.95x. PROJECT_VISION names a ptrace-cost-avoiding backend as a product
   capability and the roadmap gates the DynamoRIO prototype on a comparative benchmark, so roughly
   doubling branch-dense execution is a change to what the backend exists to provide. I named two
   concrete cheaper alternatives (an inline TLS-flag test with an out-of-line slowpath; flushing from
   the parent's post-clone callback, which unlike thread_init runs at a real application PC) and was
   explicit that I measured neither.

3. **`pending_thread_starts` is now write-only.** Declared client.c:315, incremented 4183,
   decremented 1531, read nowhere -- finding 2 removed its only reader. Delete it or print it in the
   diagnostic finding 1 needs. Small, but it is this project's recurring signature: the change
   removed a value's only consumer and left the producers.

## Credited, not faulted

The shared-state growth is safe and self-checking: the new array adds 8192 x 16 = 131,072 bytes to a
MAP_SHARED struct, every path uses `sizeof(*virtual_identity_state)`, and
`map_inherited_virtual_identity_state` refuses at client.c:1064-1066 when the inherited descriptor's
st_size disagrees, so a mixed-version attach fails closed.

The tests are unusually well guarded against passing vacuously, in three independent ways: the client
path is read with `.expect(...)` so a missing client panics rather than reporting green; the launcher
wraps drrun in `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=2s 10s` so a hang reports failure; and the test
asserts the client printed `REUSED_TID_TEST exercised=1`, so it cannot pass without reaching the race.

Determinism genuinely improves: the child's virtual TID now comes from the parent's pre-clone
allocation instead of a host-TID lookup Linux may have refilled by TID reuse (client.c:2131).

Coverage caveat: all six tests are `#[ignore]`, matching the existing convention across
reverie-dbt/tests/, so they do not run in an ordinary suite -- which also means a default suite would
not have caught finding 1.

## 3. The third-consumer hunt. This is the part worth reusing.

On 2979 the change bumped `test.detcore_unit` expected-executed from 656 to 657 for one added unit
test, and updated two files. The question that matters is not "were the two updated" but "are there
exactly two". Method, in the order I ran it:

1. **Grep the symbol, not the file.** `git grep -n "detcore_unit" <head>` across the whole tree, not
   just the paths the diff touched. The diff tells you what the author thought the consumers were;
   the grep tells you what they are.
2. **Grep the OLD value at the NEW head.** `git grep -n "\b656\b" <head> -- '*.json' '*.rs' '*.sh'
   '*.yaml' '*.toml'`. This is the step that finds the missed consumer, because a consumer the author
   did not update still carries the old number. Empty result = no stale consumer. This is the check
   that would have caught the 2694 reconstruction defect, where `ci/dag/privileged.json` said 32
   while `scripts/validate.rs` still said 24.
3. **Grep the NEW value too**, and account for every hit. On 2979 `657` appeared three times: the two
   intended updates and `TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(#657)` in `app_strict_verify.rs`, which is a pull-request
   reference and not a count. An unexplained hit is as interesting as a missing one.
4. **Look for a sibling node with the same selection.** `quick.detcore_unit` runs the same
   `-p hermit-detcore --lib --bins` crate selection as `test.detcore_unit`. I parsed
   `ci/dag/validate.json` and read its env: it carries **no** `NEXTEST_EXPECTED_EXECUTED`, so there is
   no second count to bump. Had it carried one, that would have been the missed consumer.
5. **Histogram the whole field** as a cross-check:
   `grep -o '"NEXTEST_EXPECTED_EXECUTED": "[0-9]*"' ci/dag/validate.json | sort | uniq -c`. `657`
   appears exactly once in the graph. Cheap, and it catches a count duplicated into a node you did
   not think to look at.

The same shape applies to a modified fixture: grep the fixture's *name* tree-wide, then classify each
reference as (a) encodes an expected value this change alters, or (b) inventory, selection or
documentation that only needs the name to keep existing. On 2979 the two C fixtures had sixteen
references between them and all the untouched ones were category (b), because the fixtures gained
assertions rather than being renamed, moved or removed.

## The one answer someone is waiting on

**Detcore DOES intercept and determinize `getrandom`, on every backend.** The owner's recollection
is correct and the relay ("hermit not reproducing a value its guest reads from getrandom") was
wrong. But the sharper reframing offered — an interception *with a hole* — is **also wrong**. The
interception is whole.

- Handler `detcore/src/syscalls/misc.rs:625`, fills via `fill_random_bytes` (`:465`, operative line
  `:491`) from a per-thread `Pcg64Mcg` seeded from the thread's **creation pedigree**
  (`tool_local.rs:2057` root, `lib.rs:1551` children) — not host entropy, not host Tid.
- Dispatched `lib.rs:2387`, subscribed `lib.rs:1124` inside `subscriptions()` (`lib.rs:1062`).
  Skipped **only** under `--passthru-opt`.
- Backend-independent (Detcore is the shared Reverie tool). Two additions, not exceptions: SaBRe
  detours the libc wrapper (`detcore-sabre/src/lib.rs:293`); record/replay have their own handlers
  (`hermit-cli/src/recorder/random.rs:18`, `replayer/random.rs:17`).
- Verified fresh: 12/12 runs of a direct `getrandom` guest give byte-identical draws; and in **one**
  12-run batch of the btrfs fixture the getrandom byte-hashes were identical 12/12 **while the UUID
  took two values (8 and 4)**.
- Cause of the UUID variation: libuuid XORs a `random()` mask over those bytes whose seed and
  stream position come from `gettimeofday`. The moving input is the **virtual clock** — the ~10 µs
  excursion filed separately. `strace`'s attribution to getrandom is incomplete, not wrong.

Full detail is in the task note on `btrfs-target-uuid-is-nondeterministic-under-strict` (closed).

════════ 2. THE ACTUAL STRANDING MECHANISM, AND IT IS IN THE EXIT CODE ════════
From the contract in ci-hub/ci-hub.rs:6019, verbatim:

    "Exit 0 VALIDATED, 3 FAILED (known-bad), 4 for every re-measurement state
     (TRUNCATED, NEEDS-RERUN, NO-RESULT, NOT-VALIDATED, or LEDGER-LAGGING)."
    "The distinction belongs in the verdict string and JSON, where a reader consumes
     it; the exit code stays in the refusal class where it belongs."

⚠️ SO EXIT 4 COLLAPSES FIVE OUTCOMES ON PURPOSE, and "nobody has ever measured this"
carries the SAME code as "this was measured and is bad". An agent that reads the exit
code alone cannot tell a missing measurement from a failing one -- and those need
opposite responses. The design says to read the STRING; the stranding happens when a
reader stops at the code. That is a reading hazard in a deliberately lossy signal, not
a broken query, and the fix is to consume the verdict string rather than to repair
anything.

THREE MISSING REVIEW-PROTOCOL RECORDS: SHARED CAUSE, DIFFERENT FAILURE POINTS

These are not three instances of one bad label. They share a deeper cause: the same review event is represented by independently maintained comment grammar, diagnostic strings, repository labels, and manual coordinator steps. No single operation writes and validates every record that the readers later require.

1. RETIRES was present in the canonical withdrawal comment and changes-requested-gate understood it, but approval_binding did not. That consumer mismatch is now fixed on dev-hermit main by 74b18719cad191acee8f3312a26d8896a211a85e, which shares the retirement parser and entitlement rule.

2. On https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/447, the review task instructed the reviewer to add `review-round-codex`. That is not a label in either repository and is not the reader's accepted spelling. It is only pr_status.py's human-readable missing-field string. The accepted label grammar is `adversarial-review-codex[1-4]`. A focused current-main probe shows that adding `review-round-codex` leaves codex_rounds empty and still reports missing `review-round-codex`; adding `adversarial-review-codex1` records round 1. Live PR447 currently has `passed-review-codex` but no `adversarial-review-codexN`, exactly the partially written state.

3. On https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/2694, a real Codex refusal existed without a Codex round label when the absence was reported. The direct reviewer writer, ci-hub/bin/gh --verdict, validates and posts the marker but never applies a round label. The only typed label writer, ci-hub/bin/review-attest, is coordinator-only, hardcodes APPROVED-AT, and applies both the round label and passed-review label; it cannot record a refused review. GitHub's event log shows Codex round labels were added later, at 07:53:16Z and 08:12:49Z, after the 07:47 report. That repaired the instance manually; it did not repair the missing writer.

The enumeration found two more schema mismatches:

- review-attest accepts round numbers 1 through 99, while pr_status.py and Hermit's scripts/core-review-protocol-lint.sh accept only 1 through 4. The writer accepts round 5; a focused probe shows the reader rejects `adversarial-review-claude5` as invalid.
- Hermit currently has every canonical codex/claude round label 1 through 4, plus the reader-invalid `adversarial-review-claude5`. Reverie is missing `adversarial-review-codex3` and `adversarial-review-codex4`, so review-attest must refuse those valid-by-parser rounds because it deliberately does not create labels.

Recommended repair boundary before fixing individual pull requests:

- Put the accepted round range and exact label spelling in one module consumed by review-attest and pr_status, and have the Hermit lint derive or test against the same contract.
- Make the repository-label inventory check both supported repositories against that contract.
- Provide one coordinator recording step for every completed review outcome: verify the reviewer's exact comment, apply the numbered activity label for either approval or refusal, and apply passed-review only for an approval. Today the refusal path has no typed writer.
- Make diagnostics print the exact accepted label alternatives, not the non-label shorthand `review-round-codex`.

Required tests should include: approval records activity plus approval; refusal records activity without approval; the literal `review-round-codex` does not satisfy the reader; every round accepted by the writer is accepted by the readers and exists in both repositories; an unrecorded review remains visibly incomplete.

════════ 1. AN UNATTRIBUTED REFUSAL CAN ALREADY BE RETIRED ════════
The question this task asks -- who owns a refusal nobody can be attributed -- WAS
ALREADY RULED on 2026-08-25 and is implemented in ci-hub/bin/changes-requested-gate,
the gate that actually blocks merges. A withdrawal names the refusal it retires BY
COMMENT ID (`RETIRES #<id>`), not by issuer, and `retired()` at :732 reads:

    owner = _issuer_of_comment(...)
    if owner is None:
        _retire_unowned[key] = _claimants(key)
        return True

so a refusal with no readable issuer is retirable BY ANYONE, and the gate says so out
loud rather than doing it quietly. Its own comment gives the reason: "a comment id is
assigned by GitHub and is always present, so it is the only identity that cannot go
missing." hermit#2625 is the measured case behind it.

Demonstrated, not inferred, by calling evaluate() with real comment ids:

A named issuer who has departed is a worse position than no issuer at all. No issuer
falls through to "anyone may retire, disclosed". A named issuer who is gone is matched
against a claimant list they can never join, so the refusal blocks forever and the gate
is correct to refuse -- there is no rule telling it otherwise. THE TASK TITLE NAMES THE

A fabricated marker is MARKER-SHAPED. It matches no gate, so it grants nothing --
the lucky half. But a naive scan for `APPROVED-AT: <lane> <40-hex>` COUNTS it, and
a reader skimming the thread reads the PR as approved without checking which head.
Same class as the marker-shaped EXAMPLE I had to defuse on hermit#2686 an hour
earlier, and the same class as the bare `#1234` references that produced shas
written off as permanently unmatchable.

⚠️ AND A PROSE RETRACTION DOES NOT REMOVE IT. My first correction said "withdraw
that line" and left the string in place -- three marker-shaped copies were then
live across two comments. I had to EDIT both comments to break the
`APPROVED-AT: <lane> <40hex>` shape. Verified after: 0 occurrences of the
fabricated sha, 1 marker at the real head.

# THE RULE

NEVER HAND-WRITE A 40-HEX SHA. Read it back into the text from `git rev-parse` or
`git ls-remote` in the same command that writes it. If a marker needs a full sha,
the full sha must come from a tool in that moment, not from memory or from
widening a prefix.

THE CHEAP PARTIAL: FLAG HEADS THAT TOUCH THE SAME SHARED-GLOBAL FILE
And why the cost asymmetry is the reason to prefer it over a combination gate.

NOT PROPOSED AS A DESIGN -- DEMONSTRATED. Run against the live queue 2026-08-26.

WHAT IT IS
For every open non-draft PR, take `git diff --name-only <merge-base>..<head>` and
intersect against a list of SHARED-GLOBAL paths -- files where correctness is a
property of the UNION rather than of either diff. Any path touched by two or more
heads is flagged for a human. No gate, no lock, no validate, no verdict.

     A COMPLETING full validate is 30-38 min wall (measured today: 30m03s over

and are usually fine (#2674 + #2699 were). A flag is an instruction to look, not
a refusal, and it must not be wired to block -- a blocking version would refuse
most of the queue and be routed around within a day.

through files nobody thought to enumerate are invisible to it. The list is
evidence-derived and will be incomplete until something breaks that is not on it.

comparison point. Anything else admits unreviewed lines.

═══ WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT ARGUE FOR ═══

It does NOT argue for content-addressed approvals in general. The head-binding rule exists because a
push CAN change what a reviewer read, and slackening it is how a stale approval gets credited to a
head nobody examined — the failure this row's own family of tasks was filed for.

It DOES argue that the rule currently cannot distinguish "the reviewed artefact changed" from "the
reviewed artefact did not change". A predicate that compared TREE identity across the push, and
carried an approval forward when the tree is unchanged, would have preserved both approvals here and
would still have discharged every other push on this PR — including all three rebases, which do
change the tree. I am not proposing it as a fix; option C on this row (forbid post-approval rebases)
does not cover this case at all, because this was not a rebase.

⚠️ THE SHARP POINT: MY COUNT WAS INVALIDATED BY THE AUTHOR DOING EXACTLY WHAT MY
REVIEW ASKED. Fixing a review finding adds a test; adding a test changes the
ratchet; the ratchet was pinned in a comment written before the fix existed. The
review process itself is what falsified the number. This is not carelessness
that better discipline avoids -- a correct review reliably produces it.

WHY THE WRONG VALUE IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY WRONG
A lander following "26" would have set the guard to 26 with 27 tests present.
The node asserts equality (`-ne`), so it would have gone RED -- caught. But the
same class with the inequality reversed, or a count set ABOVE the true value,
lands GREEN while permanently lowering the bar, and nothing later detects it.
The gate's own purpose is to catch a shrinking set; a hand-maintained absolute
is the one input that can shrink it silently.

TWO TRAPS THAT MAKE MANUAL RE-DERIVATION UNRELIABLE TOO
1. comm(1) reported #2694 as "removing" two tests main has. They were #2668's
   OWN tests, absent only because #2694 was based on pre-#2668 main. Not
   deletions. `main-count + PR-count` and `PR-count + delta` both give wrong
   answers; only the UNION of main's set with the PR's genuinely-new set works.
2. The PR's own manifest asserted 25 -- internally consistent for its unrebased
   base, wrong the instant it rebases. It reads like an authoritative value.

WHAT THIS SUPPORTS
Deriving the expected count at gate time (or at rebase time) rather than pinning
it removes the entire class: the collision, the staleness, and both arithmetic
traps. It also removes the need for any cross-PR coordination note, which is
what failed here -- the note was correct when written and wrong when read.

═══ WHAT THE DEFECT ACTUALLY WAS ═══

Not "KVM is nondeterministic". A guest could change the file status flags of the descriptor the
SUPERVISING hermit process was using. fcntl(F_SETFL) mutates the open file DESCRIPTION, and when
hermit passes its own stdio through, the guest's fd 2 IS hermit's fd 2, inherited in turn from
whoever ran hermit. The change outlived the guest, outlived hermit, and was there for the caller.

That is a containment defect on both backends. The KVM nondeterminism was its consequence:
--verify runs the guest twice in ONE hermit process, so run 1's mutation was still there for run 2,
which then skipped the fcntl it no longer needed and shifted every later syscall number by one.

═══ TWO FIXES, TWO LAYERS, MEASURED TO BE INDEPENDENTLY LOAD-BEARING ═══

  hermit#2694 (Detcore, covers BOTH backends). F_GETFL/F_SETFL for the container's inherited
    stdin/stdout/stderr are answered from the OpenFileDescription Detcore already maintains, seeded
    on first F_GETFL from the kernel. Detcore's read/write paths already consult that model rather
    than the kernel -- because Detcore manipulates the physical O_NONBLOCK bit itself -- so this
    routes two commands THROUGH the model instead of around it.
  reverie#494 (reverie-kvm, backend layer). host_fd(state, 2) literally returns 2, so the KVM
    executor was running guest fcntls on hermit's own descriptor. Same treatment, keyed by stream so
    dup'ed aliases share one entry.

MEASURED, not inferred: with Detcore's predicate forced false, the ptrace test fails and the KVM
test still passes (reverie catches it). With reverie's forced false and Detcore's intact, BOTH pass
(Detcore never forwards the request). With both forced false, both fail. So #2694 stands alone and
#494 is a second layer under it.
